blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Namespace is a named group inside the cluster. It comes from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: Namespaces keep each team or app's objects apart, so names can repeat in different namespaces.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name with -n shop in kubectl commands, and inside other files.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: shop

blocks.title: Add a second object
blocks.what: Three dashes start a new object in the same file. This one is a Pod.
blocks.why: Keeping the Namespace and the things inside it in one file means one command creates both.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without the dashes, both objects run together into one invalid object.
blocks.comment: A second object in the same file: a Pod
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: shop
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod

blocks.title: Put the Pod in the Namespace
blocks.what: The Pod is called web and lives in the shop Namespace.
blocks.why: Without a namespace field, kubectl puts the Pod in your current namespace, usually default.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Pod lands in the default namespace instead of shop.
blocks.comment: The Pod's name and the Namespace it lives in
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: shop
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: shop

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: One container from the nginx image, as in the first lesson.
blocks.why: A Pod needs at least one container. This block makes the file ready to apply.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without containers, Kubernetes rejects the Pod.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: shop
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: shop
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API version for this object. Namespaces and Pods are both in the core v1 API.
notes.Namespace:kind: The type of object to create. A Namespace groups objects inside the cluster.
notes.Pod:kind: The type of object to create. A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Namespace:metadata.name: The Namespace's name. It must be unique in the cluster.
notes.Pod:metadata.name: The Pod's name. It only needs to be unique within its namespace.
notes.metadata.namespace: The namespace this object lives in. It must already exist, or come earlier in the file.
notes.spec: The desired state: what you want Kubernetes to run.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.containers[].image: The image to run, with a version tag. A fixed tag runs the same version every time.

tryIt.result: Prints namespace/shop created and pod/web created.
Lists shop beside default and the system namespaces.
Deleting a Namespace also deletes everything inside it.

questions.question: Why does the Namespace come first in the file?
answers: kubectl reads files from the bottom up
The Pod goes into shop, so shop must exist first
Every file must start with a Namespace
questions.explain: kubectl creates objects in the order they appear. The Pod needs its namespace to exist already.

questions.question: Which line puts the Pod in shop?
questions.explain: namespace under the Pod’s metadata says where it lives. Line 4 names the Namespace itself.

questions.question: You run kubectl get pods without -n shop. What do you see?
answers: Only Pods in the default namespace
questions.explain: kubectl looks in the default namespace unless you name another. Add -n shop to see this Pod.

fix.message: Error from server (NotFound): error when creating "namespace.yaml": namespaces "shopp" not found
fix.explain: The Pod names a namespace that does not exist. Kubernetes creates shop, then rejects the Pod.
fix.fix: Spell it shop, to match line 4.
